summary: Boundary County, ID lookout tower first built 1963 at Faset Peak, moved to Black Mountain in 1975, and moved again about half a mile in 2019; it is not yet open to the public.

facts.design: 53-foot open timber tower with a Region 6 flat-top cab; at Black Mountain since 1975 and moved about half a mile in 2019
facts.status_note: Stands after the 2019 move. Sources disagree on whether restoration is finished: the restoration group calls the tower complete, while Campflare says it still needs restoration work before rental.

access.note: Not open to the public; Campflare lists it as not available for rental and says restoration is needed before it can open through the recreation rental program.

facts.agency: Idaho Panhandle National Forests (Kaniksu); the Idaho Department of Lands administered the site earlier

events.note: First lookout on Black Mountain: an elevated cabin on a short open timber tower (original site)
Original cabin replaced by a 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab (original site)
53-foot timber tower with Region 6 flat-top cab constructed at Faset Peak
Tower moved from Faset Peak to Black Mountain; a 1975 newspaper note records the August move
Last staffed by the Idaho Department of Lands (IDL)
Tower moved about half a mile east-northeast of the original site, with a plan to add it to the recreation rental program
Chapter supplied materials for refurbishing the relocated lookout
Work party scheduled July 20 to 22, 2025 for a pit toilet modeled on the historic outhouse and general maintenance

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and a 1975 newspaper note, quoted by Idaho Fire Lookouts, put the move in August 1975; the Idaho Fire Lookouts timeline line says 1976. 1975 is used; the 1976 date is noted.

notes_for_editor: Restoration status conflicts: the Boundary County Historic Places page calls the tower complete and awaiting rental inclusion, while Campflare says restoration work is still required. The record's coordinates (48.61354, -116.24767) are almost identical to the NHLR listing's coordinates (N 48.613497, W 116.247753), but the NHLR says the tower moved about half a mile ENE in 2019, so the coordinates may describe the old site; verify before relying on them. The FFLA 2019 report gives the chapter's refurbishment support but no restoration details. No photos added; the Idaho Fire Lookouts page carries an unlicensed photo credit, not used.
